site.name: moonlight-tickets
site.summary: moonlight-tickets-clone Fictional independent live-music ticketing platform "MoonlightTickets". Dark after-dark theme. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Discovery page: "Tonight" 4 large cards + 4-axis filters (date / genre / venue / price) + "This week" 12-event grid of fictional shows | | `event.html` | Event detail: title, time, venue, doors; favorite / share; artist bio + 3 audio clips; 3 tier cards (Early Bird / Standard / VIP with stepper -/+, VIP shows a "SELLING FAST" badge); right-side sticky order summary with fee preview; venue GA sketch SVG; accessibility notes; 3 related events | | `checkout.html` | Top 10-minute reservation countdown (<1m red pulse); collapsible cart; one accordion attendee form per ticket (First / Last / Email / e-delivery toggle, VIP adds "Name for signed poster", non-first ticket includes Copy buyer info); 3 payment methods + card-number formatting; promo (DOORS5 / TONIGHT10); right-side detailed fee breakdown (subtotal + $3.50 service × n + $2 facility × n + 3% + $0.30 processing + promo discount); Cancel second-confirmation |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full moonlight-tickets system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The MoonlightTickets platform provides a clear aesthetic and a dynamic cart experience, but several functional and usability barriers impede the user journey. The primary issues include completely non-functional event filters on the discovery page and confusing payment form behavior where alternative payment methods fail to hide credit card fields. Additionally, the checkout flow suffers from accessibility issues like unlinked form labels creating tiny tap targets, and the multi-ticket accordion pattern hides helpful utility buttons. Note that the final confirmation page was unvisited due to the destructive action blocker, and mobile layouts were under-exercised.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the ticket booking flow from event discovery to confirmation, verifying cart logic, checkout validation, and responsive adaptations.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will start on the discovery page to test filters, then navigate to an event to test ticket selection and the sticky cart. From there, it will proceed to checkout to evaluate the attendee forms, promo codes, and payment flow, ending with the confirmation page. A mobile pass will verify responsive layout and tap targets.
assumptions: Navigating from an event card on index.html loads event.html with query params (e.g., ?e=e1).
checkout.html is accessible from event.html via the 'Continue to checkout' button after selecting tickets.
Promo codes DOORS5 and TONIGHT10 are functional on the checkout page as described in the README.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets in the top navigation bar
Ticket quantity stepper buttons (-/+) and layout on mobile
Sticky order summary overlapping content on smaller screens
Checkout countdown timer behavior (under 1 minute pulse)
Multi-ticket attendee forms (Copy buyer info functionality)
Promo code application and fee breakdown calculation

phases.title: Discovery and Filtering
phases.objective: Validate event discovery and filter functionality on the home page.
key_checks: Interact with Date, Genre, Venue, and Price select filters to observe updates.
Verify navigation links and small tap targets in the header.
Click on a 'Tonight' event card and a 'This week' event card to ensure correct routing.
exit_criteria: Filters are tested and an event card is successfully clicked, loading event.html.

phases.title: Ticket Selection and Cart Logic
phases.objective: Test the ticket tier selection, constraints, and dynamic order summary.
key_checks: Use the +/- steppers to add different types of tickets (Early Bird, Standard, VIP).
Verify the 'SELLING FAST' badge on VIP tickets.
Observe the right-side sticky order summary and fee preview updating dynamically.
exit_criteria: Multiple tickets are selected, the order summary reflects the correct subtotal, and the 'Continue to checkout' button is clicked.

phases.title: Checkout Flow and Validation
phases.objective: Evaluate the checkout forms, countdown timer, and payment processing UI.
key_checks: Fill out attendee forms, testing the 'Copy buyer info' feature for secondary tickets and 'Name for signed poster' for VIP.
Apply promo codes (DOORS5 / TONIGHT10) and verify the detailed fee breakdown updates.
Interact with payment methods and test card-number formatting.
exit_criteria: Forms are validated, promo codes applied, payment details entered, and the order is submitted.

phases.title: Confirmation
phases.objective: Verify the final state of the booking process.
key_checks: Ensure the confirmation page displays the correct event, ticket quantities, and final price.
Check for any next steps or return-to-home links.
exit_criteria: Confirmation page is loaded and reviewed.

phases.title: Mobile Responsive Check
phases.objective: Re-run critical interactions on a mobile viewport to check for layout issues.
key_checks: Check header navigation tap targets on mobile.
Verify ticket stepper UI and sticky order summary behavior on event.html.
Ensure complex accordion forms on checkout.html are usable on small screens.
exit_criteria: Primary flow is completed on a mobile viewport without severe layout blockers.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit index, event, checkout, and confirmation pages.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise filtering, multi-tier ticket selection, dynamic cart updates, multi-attendee forms, promo codes, and payment validation.
coverage_targets.mobile: Execute a full booking flow on the mobile viewport to surface responsive UI issues.

notes: Pay special attention to the visual feedback of the countdown timer on checkout.html, especially as it approaches 0.
Verify if the custom SVG venue map on event.html scales correctly.

findings.user_goal: Find relevant events based on genre, date, venue, or price.
findings.problem: The dropdown filters (Genre, Venue, Price, Date) on the index page do not update the displayed event list when changed.
findings.evidence: Selecting a specific genre ('Indie rock') from the filter dropdown updates the dropdown value but fails to filter the 'This week' events list. The same non-functional behavior was observed for the Venue, Price, and Date filters.
findings.why_it_matters: Users relying on filters to find specific types of events or narrow down their options will be frustrated and may abandon the site if they have to scroll through irrelevant listings.
findings.suggestion: Implement the filtering logic to instantly update the event list upon selection, or add a prominent 'Apply Filters' button if dynamic updating is not technically feasible.

findings.user_goal: Pay using an alternative method like Apple Pay or Google Pay.
findings.problem: Selecting 'Apple-Pay-like' or 'Google-Pay-like' does not hide or disable the standard credit card entry fields. Additionally, the labels themselves use placeholder names.
findings.evidence: Selecting the 'Apple-Pay-like' payment method highlights the option but fails to hide or disable the standard credit card input fields below it. The same occurs for 'Google-Pay-like'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users will be confused about whether they still need to manually enter their credit card details after selecting an integrated wallet payment, leading to checkout friction or abandonment. Placeholder text also degrades trust.
findings.suggestion: Dynamically hide or disable the manual credit card input fields (Cardholder name, Card number, Expiry, CVC, Zip) when an alternative payment method is selected. Update the labels to production-ready names (e.g., 'Apple Pay', 'Google Pay').

findings.user_goal: Quickly fill out attendee details for multiple tickets.
findings.problem: The 'Copy buyer info from ticket 1' button is hidden inside the collapsed Ticket 2 accordion, requiring users to first discover and expand the accordion before they can use the time-saving feature.
findings.evidence: The 'Copy buyer info from ticket 1' button could not be clicked by the agent because it is hidden inside the collapsed Ticket 2 accordion.
findings.why_it_matters: Hiding helpful utility actions inside collapsed sections reduces their discoverability, forcing users to do more manual data entry if they miss the feature, increasing form friction.
findings.suggestion: Either expand all ticket attendee sections by default for small orders, or place the 'Copy buyer info' button at the header of the collapsed accordion so it is immediately visible before expansion.

findings.user_goal: Save an event to favorites or share it with friends.
findings.problem: Clicking the favorite (♡) or share (↗) buttons provides no visual feedback, state change, or confirmation message.
findings.evidence: Clicking the favorite button ('♡', ux-2) on the event page does not result in a clear state change... Clicking the share button provides no visible feedback such as a 'Copied!' toast.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on visual feedback to know if their action was successful. Without it, they may repeatedly click the button or abandon the task, feeling uncertain about the system's status.
findings.suggestion: Change the favorite icon to a filled heart (♥) when clicked, and display a temporary 'Link copied!' toast notification when the share button is activated.

findings.user_goal: Select form options easily on any device.
findings.problem: The checkboxes and radio buttons on the checkout page have a tap target of only 13x13px, indicating that their text labels are not properly linked to the inputs to expand the clickable area.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flagged the payment method radio buttons and the 'Email this ticket directly to the attendee' checkbox for having 13x13px tap targets, falling well below the 44px mobile guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets are highly frustrating on touch devices and violate accessibility guidelines, making it difficult for users with motor impairments or mobile users to complete checkout without accidental taps.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the `<input>` elements within `<label>` tags or use the `for` attribute on labels to semantically link them to the inputs. Add padding to ensure the total clickable hit area meets the 44x44px minimum.
findings.source_hint: checkout.html payment options and attendee email checkbox

findings.problem: The decrease (-) button remains fully styled and appears active even when the ticket quantity is at 0.
findings.evidence: Clicking the ticket quantity decrease button when the count is already zero correctly prevents the quantity from becoming negative. However, the button lacks a visually disabled state.
findings.why_it_matters: Presenting an interactive-looking button that does nothing when clicked violates user expectations and reduces the perceived polish of the interface.
findings.suggestion: Add a `disabled` attribute to the button when the value is 0, and style it with reduced opacity and a `not-allowed` cursor to clearly communicate its inactive state.

findings.user_goal: Explore the platform's full offerings or read policies.
findings.problem: Several links in the primary navigation and checkout footer are dead links that simply append a hash (#) to the URL.
findings.evidence: The 'Calendar', 'Artists', and 'terms' links were all observed to be dead links (`href="#"`) that do not navigate anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: Broken links diminish trust in the platform and create dead ends for users trying to learn more about upcoming events or purchase conditions.
findings.suggestion: Remove these links if the pages do not exist, or wire them up to actual content pages.
